sections.title: What This Module Covers
sections.body: This module covers the daily tooling that every Ruby developer uses on a team. You will learn: Git workflow (init, clone, add, commit, push, pull, branch, merge, rebase, stash, the .gitignore file for Ruby projects), Bundler as Ruby's dependency manager (bundle install, bundle exec, bundle update, bundle outdated), the Gemfile and Gemfile.lock (declaring gem dependencies with version constraints, the difference between the two files, when to commit each), and Rails environments (development, test, production — what changes between them, environment-specific configuration in config/environments/, and environment variables with Rails.env).

sections.title: Key Concepts at a Glance
sections.body: Git workflow: git init/clone. git status shows changes. git add -p for selective staging. git commit -m 'message'. git push origin branch-name. git pull origin main. git checkout -b feature/new-feature for a new branch. git merge branch-name. git stash / git stash pop. git log --oneline for history. Resolve conflicts: find conflict markers (<<<, ===, >>>), edit, git add, git commit. Bundler: Gemfile declares dependencies. bundle install reads Gemfile and installs. Gemfile.lock pins exact versions — always commit this in apps, never in gems. bundle exec ensures the right gem version runs. bundle update GEM_NAME updates one gem. The ~> pessimistic constraint: ~> 2.5 means >= 2.5 and < 3.0; ~> 2.5.1 means >= 2.5.1 and < 2.6. Rails environments: development (detailed errors, auto-reload, local DB). test (test DB, no logging). production (cached assets, no detailed errors, RAILS_ENV=production). RAILS_ENV and RACK_ENV env vars. database.yml has per-environment DB config. config/environments/production.rb has production-specific settings.

sections.title: What Interviewers Ask Freshers
sections.body: Key Git/Bundler fresher questions: (1) What is the difference between git merge and git rebase? (2) What should be in a Ruby project's .gitignore? (3) What is the difference between Gemfile and Gemfile.lock? Which do you commit? (4) What does bundle exec do and why is it needed? (5) What does the ~> operator mean in a Gemfile? (6) What is the difference between development, test, and production environments in Rails? (7) How do you create and switch to a new branch in Git? (8) What is a pull request and why do we use them? (9) How do you resolve a merge conflict? (10) What is RAILS_ENV and where is it used? These questions verify that you are ready to work on a team, not just write solo code.
